input.rationale: Sections 9.1 and 9.2 impose substantively identical caps on each party (greater of $100,000 or 12 months' charges paid), and Section 10 excludes consequential damages mutually while preserving Customer's payment obligations — so the cap basis, mutuality and payment-obligation points all satisfy the playbook. Indemnification payments (9.1(a)/9.2(a)) and bodily injury/property damage sit outside the cap. However, the required carve-outs for breach of confidentiality/data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement are absent, and Section 5.4/6.0 expressly makes Sections 9 and 10 prevail over the AECI for confidential information in the hosting environment, while Subsection 9.1(c)(2) excludes IBM's liability for loss of or damage to Customer's records or data altogether. That fails the fallback (which requires carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct) on a material term and is one-sided in IBM's favour. Minimal fix: a single mutual carve-out provision (new Section 9.3) leaving the existing caps intact.

proposal.summary: Add mutual carve-outs (confidentiality/data, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) outside the liability caps
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The caps in Sections 9.1/9.2 are mutual and 12-month based, which works for us, but they currently swallow confidentiality, data protection and security breaches (Section 9.1(c)(2) even excludes data loss entirely) as well as gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. We have added a single mutual carve-out provision so that those items and the Section 8 indemnities sit outside the cap, consistent with our standard position; we are happy to keep the caps themselves as drafted.

ops.text: 9.3 Exclusions from Limitations. Notwithstanding Sections 9.1, 9.2 and 10 (including Subsection 9.1(c)(2)), neither party's liability is limited or excluded in respect of: (a) a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations (including under the AECI); (b) a party's indemnification obligations under Section 8; (c) a party's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud; and (d) a party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.
